paper_metadata.title: Noise and Power Reduction in Filters Through the Use of Adjustable Biasing
paper_metadata.abstract: A technique that enables the variation of bias currents in a filter without causing disturbances at the output is presented. Thus, the bias current can be kept at the minimum value necessary for the total input signal being processed, reducing the noise and power consumption. To demonstrate this approach, a dynamically biased log-domain filter has been designed in a 0.25m BiCMOS technology. The chip occupies 0.52 mm2. In its quiescent condition, the filter consumes 575 W and has an output noise of 4.4 nA rms. Signal-to-noise ratio greater than 50 dB over 3 decades of input and total harmonic distortion less than 1% for inputs less than 2.5 mA peak are achieved. The bias can be varied to minimize noise and power consumption without disturbing the output.
